what_it_states: Real-valued (scalar) queries with sensitivity Delta q; pure epsilon-DP as main notion (Gaussian/RDP variants in Appendix F). Mechanism = compound (scale-mixture) Laplace noise whose inverse scale 1/b is randomized by a second-fold distribution; Theorem 3.1 / Appendix C: output CDF expressed through the MGF of 1/b; Theorem 4.1 (with Lemmas C.1-C.2 log-convexity of M'): epsilon = ln[E(1/b) / M'_{1/b}(-Delta q)]; Corollary 4.2 for linear combinations of independent second-fold variables; Section 4.2 usefulness optimization over the template parameters via Lagrange multipliers (Corollaries 4.3-4.4), Theorem 4.5 necessary condition to beat Laplace; Table 1 error-bound formulas for l1, l2 (root-mean-square), usefulness, Mallows, relative entropy; Algorithm 1 ensemble template (Gamma, uniform, truncated Gaussian); Appendix B case studies (Theorems B.1-B.3, B.5, B.7; Lemmas B.4, B.6, B.8 including one found by exhaustive search); Section 5 numerical/experimental comparisons with Laplace and staircase (including l1/l2 metrics, where it reports near-staircase performance and improvement for epsilon < 3 under its own setup) and a remark citing Koufogiannis et al. 2015 for a multidimensional density proportional to exp(-epsilon ||v||_2) (citation only; not opened under this direction); Appendix F Gaussian/RDP variants (Theorem F.4); Appendix G applications.
what_it_does_not_state: No optimality theorem over all noise laws (its search space is a parametric scale-mixture-of-Laplace template; coverage of 'all PDFs' is asserted only approximately and not proved); no multidimensional or l1-diamond sensitivity statement; no exact squared-Euclidean MSE value or selector for any planar model; no staircase-type or rounded-core selector; no mixed-cost all-law bound E||Z||_2^2 >= (2/3) inf E||Z||_1^2.
relation_to_SOURCE_MATCH_U1: At full coverage of this version: no T-MATCH; first failed implications = scalar query and parametric template search (scale mixtures of Laplace, continuous densities) versus an all-law planar l1-diamond optimum. The prior limit stands: the narrow proper Laplace-mixture exclusion recorded in the ledger is about this template family only and does not exclude broader mixtures or limits; full coverage adds nothing on the mixed-cost bound or MSE selection.
